## Description

In an `ImageValidatingPolicy`, `extractPayload()` fails for every admission request after the first one when the image verification cache is enabled (`--imageVerifyCacheEnabled=true`, the default):

```
Policy repro-cache-bug error: failed to evaluate policy: failed to get payload:
intoto attestation payload cannot be fetch before verifying intoto attestation
```

The cache appears to be keyed by image, so a `verifyAttestationSignatures()` call for an image already verified in this process is served from the cache and returns the signature count **without repopulating the attestation payload store**. The subsequent `extractPayload()` in the same expression then finds nothing.

This is a correctness problem rather than a performance one, because `failurePolicy: Fail` turns the evaluation error into a **denial**. An image that fully satisfies the policy is admitted once and rejected from then on, with a message that reads like a genuine policy violation. Setting `--imageVerifyCacheEnabled=false` is the only workaround I found.

Possibly a side effect of #16657.

Kyverno needs `--imageVerifyCacheEnabled=true` (default). The image below is public

## Description

In `pkg/cli/loader/resource_loader.go`, the `executeTasks` method uses a `for` loop to wait for results from a worker pool. Inside this loop, a `select` statement has a timeout case using `time.After`:

```go
for i := 0; i < expectedResults; i++ {
    select {
    // ...
    case <-time.After(cl.resourceOptions.Timeout):
    // ...
    }
}
```

Using `time.After` inside a loop or frequent select statement causes a memory leak because the underlying `time.Timer` is not garbage collected until it expires. If `executeTasks` processes a large number of tasks (e.g. 10,000 resources), this will allocate 10,000 timers on the heap that all hang around until `cl.resourceOptions.Timeout` (which could be minutes) is reached, unnecessarily inflating memory usage.

## What we ruled out

- **By design**: `time.After` is a known anti-pattern in Go loops.

## Expected behavior

The code should use a reusable `time.Timer` via `time.NewTimer(timeout)` outside the loop and call `timer.Reset()` on each iteration. This guarantees that only one timer allocation exis

### Problem

When multiple admission requests verify the same image concurrently, each cache miss starts an independent remote image/signature verification. A burst therefore duplicates registry manifest, signature, and transparency-log work before the first successful request can populate Kyverno's verification cache.

The fan-out increases registry load and produces long-tail admission latency. It also affects rules with `useCache: false`, where there is intentionally no persistent result cache but identical in-flight work can still be shared safely.

### Proposed solution

Add a process-local singleflight coordinator around image verification, keyed by the existing verification identity:

- policy UID and resource version;
- rule name;
- normalized image reference.

On a persistent-cache miss, the flight leader should recheck the cache, perform the remote verification once, and populate the cache only on success. Concurrent waiters should receive value copies of the same result. Waiters must remain independently cancellable, and failed verification results must not be persisted.

The same coordinator should coalesce in-flight operations when `useCache: false`; only the persisten
title: [Performance] Coalesce concurrent image verification requests

## Bug Description

In `pkg/engine/apicall/executor.go`, the `executeServiceCall` method passes a **nil `http.ResponseWriter`** to `http.MaxBytesReader` when limiting service API call response sizes:

```go
// executor.go line 91-94
var w http.ResponseWriter  // nil — never assigned

if a.config.maxAPICallResponseLength != 0 {
    resp.Body = http.MaxBytesReader(w, resp.Body, a.config.maxAPICallResponseLength)
}
```

This has two problems:

### 1. Potential nil pointer panic

`http.MaxBytesReader` uses the `ResponseWriter` internally to signal connection closure when the limit is exceeded. When the response body exceeds `maxAPICallResponseLength`, the internal `maxBytesReader.Read()` method attempts to call `requestTooLarge()` on the `ResponseWriter`, which will **panic on the nil pointer**. This means any service API call that returns a response larger than the configured limit will crash the Kyverno admission controller process.

### 2. Wrong abstraction — `http.MaxBytesReader` is for servers, not clients

### Describe the bug

In `pkg/controllers/admissionpolicygenerator/controller.go` and `pkg/controllers/webhook/validating.go`, the cancellable context provided by the Kubernetes controller-runtime is being discarded when checking feature toggles. Instead, `context.TODO()` is passed to `toggle.FromContext()`. 

This is problematic because:
1. It breaks the toggle system if toggles are overridden or injected into the root context at application startup (the controller drops the context and falls back to dynamic defaults).
2. It drops the cancellable context (`ctx`), which is considered an anti-pattern as it prevents proper teardown/cancellation signaling if the toggle retrieval block were to ever wait.

```go
// Current implementation

// Should be
generateValidatingAdmissionPolicy := toggle.FromContext(ctx).GenerateValidatingAdmissionPolicy()
```

In `pkg/engine/engine.go`, functions like `Validate`, `Mutate`, `Generate`, and `ApplyBackgroundChecks` receive a request-scoped `context.Context`. However, when checking if the policy applies to the resource via `internal.MatchPolicyContext()`, the live context is dropped.

Part of #16302 (1.19 — feature parity + hard deprecation of legacy `kyverno.io` policy types).

## Problem Statement

The legacy `kyverno.io` policy types are deprecated in 1.19 and planned for removal in 1.20, but the Kyverno Helm chart does not surface any deprecation notice for the legacy CRDs. Users installing/upgrading via Helm get no indication of the upcoming removal.

## Solution Description

Add a deprecation notice for legacy CRDs to the Helm chart, for example:

- `NOTES.txt`: print a deprecation warning on install/upgrade when legacy CRDs are enabled, naming the replacement `policies.kyverno.io/v1` types and linking to the migration guide.
- Chart `README`/values documentation: mark legacy CRD values (`crds.*` for `kyverno.io` types) as deprecated with removal targeted for 1.20.
- Consider annotating the legacy CRD manifests (e.g. a `deprecated.kyverno.io` annotation) so the deprecation is visible on the installed objects.
- Optionally add a values toggle to allow opting out of installing legacy CRDs ahead of 1.20.

## Additional Context

Required before the 1.19 release cut ("Helm chart deprecation notice for legacy CRDs" checklist item in #16302).
title: [Feature] Helm chart deprecation notice for legacy kyverno.io CRDs
